question: May I release this combined repair batch if all other checks pass, while keeping the existing development-tool security warning open? This would be a one-time exception; the production dependencies have no reported vulnerability.
answer: Yes, release if all other checks pass

scope.batch: Combined sitewide country/pricing, phonebook/CCINFO, Outlook groups, SPC transaction, backup validation and related register/navigation repairs
scope.classification: Existing development-only code-checking dependency; deeply nested crafted patterns can exhaust the stack

conditions: All other functional, type, build, access-control, contract and release checks must pass on the final combined source.
Rerun unchanged full and production dependency audits on the final PR head. Any other advisory or failed check is outside this exception.
Keep the warning and failed full-audit evidence visible; do not disable, suppress or weaken scanners, deployment protections or branch requirements.
Verify the canonical account, repository, database, Vercel team/project and immutable release revision; preserve the user's dirty checkout and already-live Azure worker.
Apply only reviewed additive migrations and verify a staged production build before promotion; report remaining verification limits honestly.
notAuthorizedByThisException: Any other failed release check or security finding
Any unrelated production data, contact, account, email, financial or cloud configuration change
A dependency downgrade, unreviewed upgrade or recurring waiver
A claim that the advisory is fixed, the whole site is bug-free or disaster recovery has been demonstrated
followUp: Keep the development dependency warning open and reassess compatible updates. This exception applies only to this combined repair release.
